## MAX_OUTSTANDING_UPLOAD_BYTES_PER_SUBJECT variable

Most bytes one subject can have received across its outstanding uploads: 512 MiB.

**Signature:**

```typescript
MAX_OUTSTANDING_UPLOAD_BYTES_PER_SUBJECT: number
```

## Remarks

Smaller than [MAX_OUTSTANDING_UPLOADS_PER_SUBJECT](./runtime.max_outstanding_uploads_per_subject.md) times [MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES](./runtime.max_upload_bytes.md) on purpose: a caller may stage a few large files or many small ones, but never 1.6 GiB at once. A write that would exceed it fails with `TransferError` `too-large`<!-- -->, and its partial bytes are deleted.

Only outstanding uploads count: bytes of uploads that have expired but not yet been swept, and of consumed uploads not yet released, do not. So the bytes a subject has on disk are bounded but can briefly exceed this budget, until the next sweep (at most a minute after expiry, given activity) or the end of [CONSUMED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_MS](./runtime.consumed_upload_retention_ms.md)<!-- -->. A receive in progress counts in steps of up to 1 MiB, so a concurrent receive by the same subject may be refused up to that much early.
